target: V167 transfers exact target-body authored weights onto connected jacket sleeves, bodice, and collar in one neutral rest-pose basis. It averages weights across shared canonical sewn vertices, constrains Cloth only to declared shared seams, and restores sewn boundary positions to the captured neutral rest coordinates after baking under a 15 mm per-vertex correction cap. This is a disposable construction hypothesis; fit, appearance, and release stay unapproved.

researchTrial.method: Validate hash-bound construction inputs, manufacture an editable 3D prototype, and directly review its rendered appearance before completion.
researchTrial.review: The concept shows jacket, overskirt, and shorts appearance; it does not establish sewing order, dimensions, allowance, fabric stretch, avatar fitting, or deformation.

bodyProfileEvidence.evidenceBoundary: Neutral and repository-defined Large body cross-sections only. Reuse is bound to the same byte-identical SiroinoSotai PC FBX; waistline selection, garment ease, collar circumference, shape-key coverage, fit, and motion remain unapproved.

releaseBoundary: Prototype geometry only. Rendered visualAppearanceReview, fit, runtime, and customer release evidence remain unverified and mandatory before release.

shapeKeyTransfer.evidenceBoundary: Transfers only the declared body-size keys from the exact source triangle used for weight mapping. It records source and output mesh evidence; it does not claim smoothness, evaluated fit, Unity import compatibility, or release acceptance.

jacket-sleeves.reason: The V163 direct pose review found jacket sleeves hanging away from T-pose, raised and crossed arms. The body collider was armature-animated while sleeve panels entered Cloth without that armature deformation, so the simulated body and garment did not share a moving rest-space basis. V164 measured 7.06 mm divergence at a shared sleeve/bodice seam after transferring only sleeve weights. V165 exposed a pin-selection defect: all sleeve vertices received Cloth Pin because armature weight groups already existed.
jacket-sleeves.evidenceBoundary: For the disposable 48-frame native Cloth pose sweep only, interpolate the exact imported target body's authored vertex-group weights over its nearest surface triangle, add the target armature modifier before Cloth, and enable dynamic mesh evaluation. Cloth pin IDs are restricted to Image2Outfit Cloth Pin seam membership. Stage 09 independently recalculates and audits production garment weights. This does not prove sleeve fit, collision safety, motion acceptance, appearance, or release readiness.

jacket-bodice.reason: Sleeve-only skinning created a 7.06 mm divergence at a shared sewn vertex. Connected bodice and collar panels must use the same target skeleton and seam-averaged weights so armscye and shoulder seams remain in one deformation basis.
jacket-bodice.evidenceBoundary: Transfer target-body weights onto connected bodice and collar panels and synchronize each shared canonical sewn vertex to the mean of participating panel weights before posing. These non-cloth pose previews are construction diagnostics only and do not establish fit, garment motion acceptance, appearance, or release readiness.

prototypeSharedSeamAnchor.reason: V166 Cloth baking moved shared sleeve/bodice boundary points and the canonical skin exporter rejected a 7.06 mm divergence. Correct only shared canonical seam vertices to their measured pre-solve neutral positions; fail if any individual correction exceeds 15 mm.
prototypeSharedSeamAnchor.evidenceBoundary: The actual pre-restore seam gap, number of changed shared references, maximum and mean per-reference correction, and post-restore gap are recorded. This is a capped prototype seam-continuity operation at the neutral export frame, not a pose-fit, appearance, fabric, or release acceptance.

poseResponseTrial.evidenceBoundary: Prototype-only Blender Cloth timeline with the actual target armature driving the collision body and the shared overskirt waist pins before Cloth evaluation. Posed customer renders continue to use the exported rest-shape skinning path; this trial does not create runtime cloth, and does not prove fit or collision safety.

clothSimulation.evidence: V167 transfers authored target-body bone groups onto connected jacket sleeves, bodice and collar before pose simulation, averages weights at shared canonical seam vertices, and applies the shared armature in one neutral rest basis before Cloth. Cloth pins use only declared attachment seam vertices; sleeves are evaluated as a dynamic mesh against the moving collision body. After baking, only shared sewn boundary coordinates are restored to their captured neutral positions under the declared 15 mm per-vertex cap, with before/after gaps and correction statistics recorded. It records mapped coverage, pin counts, surface distances, seam-gap diagnostics, pose hashes and regenerated renders. The saved garment remains prototype-only; this does not export runtime Cloth or grant fit, collision safety, appearance, or release acceptance.
clothSimulation.reason: V163 directly showed moving avatar poses but sleeves displaced from T-pose, raised, and crossed arms; V164's sleeve-only weight transfer created a measured 7.06 mm seam gap. V165 mapped connected jacket panels through the target-body skeleton but accidentally treated every newly weighted sleeve vertex as a Cloth pin. V166 restricted pin membership to the named Cloth Pin group, but actual neutral Cloth bake still produced a measured 14.1 mm shared seam gap and skin/export rejected it. V167 applies a measured, explicitly capped correction only to shared sewn boundary vertices before downstream skin transfer. Inspect freshly regenerated current pose renders if the pipeline advances; skirt poses remain a separate review. This sweep is prototype diagnostics only, not a fit, coverage, collision-safety, appearance, or release pass.

jacket-sleeves.reason: Direct review shows excessive sleeve wrinkling in the neutral render. Compare a structured sleeve cloth setting with the existing 0.45 baseline; 2.2 is a local prototype trial value, not a Lilac fabric calibration.
jacket-sleeves.evidenceBoundary: One neutral 48-frame trial against the current jacket sleeve panels; this parameter experiment does not establish fit, motion, material behavior, appearance approval, or release readiness.

jacket-sleeves.reason: Direct neutral and pose renders still show physical sleeve corrugation after the bounded cloth solve. Compare a low-strength interior-only fairing pass while locking all open garment boundaries and sewn pins.
jacket-sleeves.evidenceBoundary: Three post-bake uniform Laplacian iterations at factor 0.18 on non-boundary sleeve vertices only. Exact source, displacement statistics, fixed-boundary count, and resulting mesh hashes are recorded by this run. This is a geometry hypothesis only; it does not establish fit, fold quality, motion, appearance approval, or release readiness.

frontClosure.construction: Right-front hem crosses center by 40 mm in local pattern coordinates, tapering to zero at the upper opening; left front supplies continuous underlay to center. Existing shoulder and side seams retain their common vertices.
frontClosure.evidenceBoundary: Corrects a cut-away lower front into an actual overlap hypothesis. 40 mm extension and 2 mm spacing are design hypotheses, not avatar-approved ease. Closure anchoring, dynamic overlap separation, trim and final fit remain unverified.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V80 keeps the connected-panel profile shared across overskirt panels to preserve seam continuity while reducing thigh attachment to the legs in seated/crouch poses. Uncalibrated prototype hypothesis only.

weightProfile.evidenceBoundary: V146 changes the rest-pose geometry path for the sewn front-lap panels by placing them against measured UpperLeg_L/UpperLeg_R deform surfaces with seam fades. The placement is not shape-key fit, motion, collision, seam, visual, or release evidence.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V91 keeps the four shorts panels and gusset on the existing experimental weight profile. The generated surface-copy thigh covers are excluded from that profile so their vertices retain barycentric source-body skin weights. This is an uncalibrated prototype hypothesis and grants no fit or appearance acceptance.

weightProfile.evidenceBoundary: Existing V85 prototype distribution is carried onto the V87 gusset for skinning coverage only; no change to measured behavior is claimed. Seam strain, crotch deformation, weight continuity and pose response remain unverified.

prototypeWeightRegions.evidenceBoundary: V91 transfers each copied thigh-cover vertex from the nearest eligible target-avatar body triangle with barycentric source skin weights, without the shorts-panel weight profile. The shell is only an offset copy of neutral body surface; transfer accuracy in motion, seam continuity, fit and shape-key response remain unverified.
